newsitem.title: UK: Iraq Kirkuk June price rise faces little resistance.
newsitem.headline: Iraq Kirkuk June price rise faces little resistance.

text.p: Prices for Iraqi Kirkuk crude oil exports will rise in June in line with Saudi term price increases announced on Monday but Baghdad should face little resistance from customers with May barrels still commanding healthy spot market premiums.

The first 180-day period of the United Nations oil-for-food deal, allowing Iraq to sell up to $2 billion worth of oil to raise money for humanitarian imports, expires on June 7 but diplomats expect it to be renewed for another six months.

State Saudi Aramco told European customers on Monday it was lifting the June price formula for Arab Light by 20 cents to Dated Brent less $2.05 a barrel. It left the U.S. price unchanged at WTI less $3.60.

Kirkuk Blend, which is linked on a cent-for-cent basis with Arab Light under arrangements established by the United Nations, will be priced 20 cents higher in June at Dated Brent less $2.00 a barrel for Europe. U.S. customers will still pay WTI less $3.65.
"This should have very little impact but it all depends on what happens to the value of (rival Russian) Urals," said a European customer of Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO).
"With Urals still around (dated Brent) minus $1.00 then Kirkuk still looks very good at (dated Brent) minus $2.00," he added.

Kirkuk has traded recently at about 25 cents a barrel over the May Official Selling Price (OSP) of Dated Brent less $2.20 and last week one of the few cargoes loading this month and still unsold was on offer last week at OSP +40 cents.

When the U.N. deal was implemented last December, traders were reluctant to pay the initial OSP of Dated Brent less $1.55 a barrel. Even after Monday's Saudi price rise, customers will still be paying 45 cents a barrel less and are keen to lay their hands on as many barrels as possible.

Term lifters say the Iraqi grade, which has made European buyers a tidy profit in May thanks to a recovery in refining margins and delays to Russian exports at the Black Sea port of Novorossiisk, will lose none of its allure in June unless Urals falls back to around Dated Brent less $1.30/$1.40 a barrel.

Even then, a narrow spread between high and low sulphur fuel oil in the Mediterranean -- currently at around $10.50 a tonne against the 1997 average of $12.65 -- could still tip the balance in Kirkuk's favour, term customers said.
"If this situation doesn't change then Kirkuk will still be the best option," said one.
Kirkuk exports in May are expected to rise slightly to around 445,000 barrels per day (bpd) from an original 430,000 bpd programme for April.
Full Iraqi exports under the oil sale, including sales of Basrah Light from Iraq's Gulf terminal at Mina al-Bakr, have been running at around 750,000 bpd in recent weeks.

Liftings in early June are expected to be light, however, with SOMO's customers reporting pressure to load all barrels covered by contracts for the first six months of the deal by the end of May. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
